Growing in Grace
GROH-ing in GRAYS
verbal phrase
From the Greek auxanō (to grow, increase) joined with charis (grace); the believer's progressive increase in grace and knowledge.

Biblical Definition

Growing in grace is the believer's progressive increase in holiness, faith, and the knowledge of Christ throughout the whole course of the Christian life. Peter closes his epistle with the command, grow in grace, and in the knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ—a charge that joins inward growth to a deepening apprehension of Christ Himself. This growth is the fruit of regeneration and the work of sanctification: having been born again by the incorruptible seed of the Word, the believer desires the sincere milk of the Word that he may grow thereby. It is gradual and progressive, not instantaneous; the path of the just is as the shining light, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day. Yet it is real, for God who began the good work will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ. The means are appointed: the Word, prayer, the sacraments, fellowship, and the providential discipline of God, all wielded by the Spirit to mortify sin and quicken graces. Such growth is not the believer's own achievement but the operation of grace within him, even as he works out his salvation with fear and trembling because God works in him both to will and to do. The marks of it are increasing humility, deepening love, sharper hatred of sin, and a fuller delight in Christ. Thus the saint, though never sinless in this life, is ever being conformed more closely to the image of his Lord until grace is consummated in glory.

Webster 1828 Definition

The believer's progressive increase in grace, holiness, and the knowledge of Christ.

expand to see more

GROWING IN GRACE, verbal phrase. From the Greek auxanō, to grow or increase, joined with charis, grace.

The progressive increase of the believer in holiness, faith, and the knowledge of Christ.

The ongoing fruit of regeneration and the work of sanctification in the soul.

Peter commands in 2 Peter 3:18, "But grow in grace, and in the knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ."

A gradual and lifelong work, real yet never complete until consummated in glory.

Key Scripture

2Pe 3:18 — "But grow in grace, and in the knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ. To him be glory both now and for ever. Amen."

1Pe 2:2 — "As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby:"

Pro 4:18 — "But the path of the just is as the shining light, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day."

Phi 1:6 — "Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ:"

Modern Corruption

Sanctification is recast as self-improvement, instant perfection, or mere positive change apart from grace.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. Yet growing in grace is often distorted within the church. Some make it a program of self-help and self-improvement, a matter of human effort and technique rather than the work of the Spirit. Others swing to perfectionism, claiming a sudden entire sanctification that Scripture nowhere promises in this life, while still others deny progressive growth altogether, presuming upon grace while remaining content in sin.

To recover the truth we must hold that growth in grace is genuine, gradual, and wrought by God. The believer truly increases in holiness and the knowledge of Christ, yet this increase is the operation of grace within him, even as he diligently uses the means God has appointed. He works out his salvation because God works in him to will and to do. So the Christian neither despairs at slow progress nor presumes upon a perfection not yet given, but presses on, confident that He who began the good work will complete it in glory.

Hebrew Roots

Growing in grace is the progressive, Spirit-wrought increase of the regenerate soul toward Christ.

expand to see more

Growth in grace flows from regeneration and is the work of sanctification.

It is progressive and lifelong, not instantaneous or perfected in this life.

It is wrought by God through appointed means: Word, prayer, sacraments, and providence.

The believer labors in it because God works in him both to will and to do.

Its marks are deeper humility, love, hatred of sin, and delight in Christ.

Usage

"The believer uses the means of grace diligently that he may grow thereby."

"Pastors call the saints to grow in grace and in the knowledge of their Lord."

"Slow progress drives the Christian to grace rather than to despair."
